english: Congratulations! You have met the goals of your merchant marine and built for them enough ships and docks to empower their plans. Please choose a reward from among the benefits your new trading empire is able to provide to you.

Our trade empire should be leveraged in to producing lots of wealth.
Our ship captains gain extra experience, enabling them to better navigate.

Our eldest scholars have collaborated on an effort to collect, record, and preserve all of our oral traditions and unwritten literature.[PARAGRAPH:1]They require storage space for pottery, stone tablets and other artifacts, as well as special repositories within our cities.
%s1_civ scholars have successfully recorded all of their oral traditions and stories in to a new compendium of literature, thereby completing the quest of Classic Literature!

Congratulations! You have met the goals of your scholars and built for them enough [COLOR_BUILDING_TEXT]Libraries[COLOR_REVERT] to store their newly recorded works. Please choose a reward from among the benefits your new treasure trove of written literature are able to provide to you.

Use the leagues to make your people happy.
Leverage these sports leagues in to a cultural tradition.
Organize  large-scale periodic sporting events in the name of Zeus.

Our war against the %s1:2_civ_adjective continues. Our spiritual leaders cry out for us to wage a crusade to wrest control of %s6_city away from them.
Crusade[PARAGRAPH:1]You are tasked by your religious leaders to capture and occupy the Holy City.
[PARAGRAPH:1]You will fail this quest if a rival civilization captures %s1_city first, if you change your state religion, or if your war ends for any reason prior to your success.

Congratulations! Your Crusade to secure the sacred lands of %s2_city has wrested control of the city away from the %s1:2_civ_adjective! Please choose a reward from among the benefits that may accrue from the joy your people feel in this successful Crusade.
%s1_civ_adjective armies have completed their Crusade, wresting control of the Holy City of %s2_city away from the %s4_civ_adjective people!
Your Crusade has ended. The quest has failed.
The Holy City needs more protection. Recruit and train capable units from among the faithful.
[ICON_BULLET]Add %d1 [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]%s2_unit[COLOR_REVERT] [NUM1:defender:defenders] to %s3_city.
Harness the fervor of the believers to construct a Holy Shrine to honor the sacred sites where our faith was born.
[ICON_BULLET]Build [COLOR_BUILDING_TEXT]%s1_building[COLOR_REVERT] in %s2_city.
Spread the word of our success and of the blessings of our faith as far and wide as possible.
[ICON_BULLET]Spread [COLOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]%s1_religion[COLOR_REVERT] to up to %d2 new [NUM2:city:cities].
A miracle performed at the city wall in %s2_city is attracting %s3_religion_adjective pilgrims from far and wide.
A miracle is believed to have occurred at the city wall in %s2_city. Pilgrims are flocking from all over to visit the new holy site.
The tourism will enhance city revenue.
We should hire and train some of the pilgrims as missionaries.
A renowned playwright from %s2_city is attracting patrons and fans from far and wide.
A prolific playwright from %s2_city has written a long series of exceptionally popular plays. His home theatre has gained renown.
The theatre patronage will enhance city revenue.
We could double the cultural value of the theatre by officially sanctioning this artist's works.
A %s1_civ_adjective gladiator from %s2_city has become a local hero and an inspiration.
A gladiator from %s2_city has survived many battles in the arena. He is attracting a lot of fans.
No one survives forever. Cash in on the phenomenon before he meets the inevitable end.
Arrange for him to be matched against easy opponents and see that his legend increases.
A cache of ancient texts has been discovered hidden away in a %s1_civ_adjective monastery.
A cache of ancient writings has been discovered hidden away in a cubby hole in a monastery in %s2_city!
Hand the material over to our researchers.
Preserve these works as a cultural treasure.
A warlord from %s2_city has made a generous contribution to his community.
An esteemed warlord who operates from the castle in %s2_city has offered to set up a special military academy at his own expense.
We have no need of his services. Ask him instead to donate his money to the state.
Excellent! Have him train Pikeman units for us.
Superb! Have all our military recruits in that city undergo a training regimen at the new academy.
Vermin got in to the granary in %s2_city. All the food stored there was ruined.
Vermin have gotten in to the granary in %s2_city. All the food stored there is spoiled.
That sounds like bad news, but what can we do? Nothing.
Pay to have the lost grain replaced.
The hospital in %s2_city is gaining favor among the pious because it is believed to be blessed by a spirit angel.
Rumors that a spirit angel of mercy is watching over the patients in the hospital in %s2_city are leading many devout believers to seek treatment there.
The extra patients will enhance city revenue.
We could sanction the hospital as a state holy site. This may please the local populace.
A pilot from %s2_city has inspired pride amongst the %s1_civ_adjective people by becoming the first to fly solo over the North Pole.
A pilot from %s2_city has become the first to fly solo over the North Pole and return safely.
Set up a monument at the airport to produce tourism.
An industrial accident started a fire that gutted the Factory in %s2_city.
A fire at the Factory in %s2_city, which was started by a worker's mistake, has gutted the building.
Emphasize improved safety so that this particular type of accident should never happen again.
Fund an emergency rebuilding effort.
A scientific breakthrough at the laboratory in %s2_city is credited in part to the free flow of ideas and information nurtured by the %s1_civ_adjective government.
A scientific breakthrough has occurred at the Laboratory in %s2_city.
This should speed our current research.
A retiring %s1_civ_adjective naval captain has pledged his expertise to assist the Drydock located in %s2_city.
A retiring captain from one of our most elite naval vessels has pledged his wisdom and abilities toward shipbuilding at the drydock in %s2_city.
The reputation boost should enhance revenues.
We should fund an effort to translate his experience into a format that can be passed on to future generations.
The thoroughly religious %s1_civ_adjective state is dealing with an outbreak of heresy in some segments of its population.
A heretical spiritual movement has started in %s2_city and is gaining strength among some sections of our populace.
Suppress the heresy! Then launch a drive to remind our people that we already adhere to the one true faith.
Tolerate the heresy, yet reward the faithful with reduced taxes for a while, to send a message.
Ignore the heresy.

The %s1_civ_adjective people from the city of %s5_city have seen their homes burned! They are rising up against the wicked %s4_civ_adjective invaders, forming Partisan units to join the resistance as militia fighters!
Our city of %s6_city has been destroyed by the rampaging %s1_civ_adjective army. Some of our citizens are forming partisan resistance!
Send word to the new partisan units to continue the fight near their destroyed homes.
%s1_civ_adjective citizens from the city we just razed are taking to the surrounding countryside to form Partisan resistance units!
Receive %d1 [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]%s2_unit[COLOR_REVERT] [NUM1:unit:units] near the ruins of the city.

Although we will lose up to half their number to exhaustion, desertion and willful refusal to leave the area, we must convince these units to retreat. Have them march to our capital city, where they will reform into units.
%s1_civ_adjective citizens from the city we just razed are fleeing toward their capital and are expected to form Partisan resistance units there!
Receive %d1 [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]%s2_unit[COLOR_REVERT] [NUM1:unit:units] in our capital city of %s3_city.
The %s1_civ_adjective hereditary dynasty has died out. A new faction has claimed the throne and is off to a roaringly successful start.
The old dynasty has died out! No more hereditary heirs remain to claim the throne!
Throw support behind the leading general to become the new monarch via coup d'état.
Let the nobles fight amongst themselves. The strongest or cleverest will emerge as the new monarch.
Follow the guidance of spiritual leadership in identifying who enjoys divine favor, then support that claimant.
Scandal has thrown the %s1_civ_adjective senate in to chaos. A constitutional crisis has emerged. Yet this also opens the door to political reforms.
The eldest senator of the leading opposition party has been disgraced by scandal. The entire senate has been thrown into chaos.
Let the senators fight amongst themselves. When both sides are weakened, step in and assert presidential authority.
Support the ruling party in impeaching numerous members of the scandalized party, destroying all effective opposition to the ruling party.
Rely on judicial authority to enforce the letter of the constitution.
%s1_civ_adjective election results were so close, the courts had to rule on the vote-counting procedures to arrive at an outcome.

Election results are so close, they fall within the margin of error typically written off to system inadequacies such as lost or mismarked ballots, hanging chads, or counting errors. With no indisputable way to decipher the true vote count, the election's outcome has been placed in the hands of the courts.

Let the court case take its course, even if the judges seem to split their vote along a purely partisan basis. Follow the constitution to its letter, even though the outcome appears to come down to which party in the dispute had more supporters on the bench.

Refuse to submit to constitutional rule of law, citing wishful reinterpretations of the constitution or arguments based on passion and principle. Arrive at the desired outcome without heed to the actual constitution.
A charismatic %s1_civ_adjective dictator has risen to control the Party. This strong man is reshaping the government to suit his plans.
A stronger, more charismatic dictator has seized control of the Party and the nation!
Advise him to focus on his relationship with the armed forces.
Advise him to focus on domestic harmony and stamping out sources of opposition.
Friendly locals have granted sanctuary to a wounded %s1_civ_adjective unit.
A wounded %s1_civ_adjective unit has received assistance from a small faction who resists the rule of their enemy.
A pious tribe who believe in mercy have extended religious protection to a wounded unit of %s1_civ_adjective origin.
A small tribe of friendly locals have granted sanctuary to our beleaguered %s3_unit.
This assistance should help our unit recover its strength.

Congratulations! Your Greed is unmatched! You have managed to wrest control of the coveted %s1_civ_adjective [COLOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]%s9_resource[COLOR_REVERT] resource! Your generals are already expanding their military planning.

From among our most faithful knights emerges one with holy vision.

Then our troops may land on the same day the battle begins and thrust inland against a foe who will be in total disarray.

Our intent is to keep the peace through strength. Leverage our might in to commercial opportunity.

Our game designers have developed a new addictive game of Civilization. How shall we proceed?
Send congratulations to the developers. Our people should enjoy this game.
This game seems to have great educational potential. Suggest that it be used in our educational system.
Computer games? They have no place in our society! Sell the franchise to foreign buyers!
Sir, our slaves are on the verge of revolting! As long as our society continues to use slaves, there is a possibility of them revolting!
The slaves of %s2_city are on the verge of revolt!
Inspired by books telling stories about the culture of %s2_city, immigrants are flowing to the city!
Immigrants are flowing to %s2_city inspired by stories of its culture!
%s1_civ_adjective herbalists have discovered a plant that might result in better illness treatment.
Our herbalists have discovered a new plant that holds great promise for health treatments. However, tests on human subjects are required to find the right mixture.
Forget these tests. Anything worth knowing has already been discovered, so why risk needless death?
Alright, try limited tests, but only on non-essential citizens.
Health is the bedrock to world domination! Run full scale tests on all but the youngest and weakest among us.
In their attempts to find the right mixture of herbs, our healers caused fatalities throughout the empire!
Our experiments have been a success! Our cities now enjoy better healing herbs!
Our experiments have been a resounding success! We now posess much better treatments!
A great beast has been discovered near one of our hunting camps.
Let it breed and give offspring. Hunt sparingly.
Looks like it could feed many people. Organize a hunting party!

You may keep your gods and rituals, your codes and your honor. Why should I care for obscure promises of afterlife rewards and the merits of virtue, when I've got a whole cellar full of pure, liquid bliss encased in glass and wood?-Dengrahl Lern, Merchant
The Azer are the eyes of Bhall in Erebus. She has sent them into creation to learn what has changed while she slept during the Age of Ice.

A Beast of Agares is a living beast that has gone through an unholy ritual that strengthens it. The ritual involves massive human sacrifice. Beasts of Agares enjoy hunting paladins, and can sense the presence of one from miles away.

In later generations of the Age of Rebirth, most armies would deploy detachments of brutal men fueled by bloodlust called berserkers. Battle rage makes their surroundings disappear as they tear away their opposition armed with a pair of hand axes. These elite units are inspired by legends from the Age of Ice, legends of men who carried an axe in each hand.

Of the beasts formed by men only the centaurs retain some part of their noble nature. Many creatures were made from the bodies of men, but they were of ten reduced to the passions of their bestial form.  Perhaps it is because the animal they were made from, the majestic stallions of the Cerici, were known for their docile nature as well as their strength. But do not assume that the Centaurs are passive. Those creeping into their glades expecting gentle pacifists bounding away like deer when they see strangers will be surprised by the firm, battle-hardened giants they find.  Centaurs are fond of war paint and other body art, thick, dangerous weapons, and feasts of wild fruit and meat so undercooked it drips with blood.
I am the firmament upon which creation was laid. What sword can harm me? What wall can resist my strength?-Granik, earth elemental
A mix of eagles and lions, griffons make loyal mounts and pets to those who are able to tame them. They enjoy dangerous flying so less reckless riders will probably only ride a griffon once.

These demons, also called "Drinkers", consume the souls of their victims becoming more powerful each time they kill someone. After a few kills the ira becomes so powerful opponents are better served to hide until they return to normal rather than try to kill it. Calming spells are very effective against ira, and weaken them considerably.

Lions with wings and tails that can fire iron spikes larger than a crossbow bolt. A full grown manticore stands nearly seven feet at the shoulder. Manticores have a voracious appetite and there are few whocan afford to feed them when they are kept as guards. Likewise they are likely to overhunt their territory when living in the wild and are unable to settle in one area.
A minotaur is a tall humanoid with the head of a bull. They are vigilant guardians, and outside of being unable to resist a fight they mind they are reliable soldiers.

Once human, the mobius witches live in the bizarre between worlds of Ceridwen. In Erebus they have an odd fascination with edges, corners and doorways,sometimes to the point of fearing them. Though they display little interest in relationships with humans or with each other they are as insightful to the nature of relationships as they are obtuse about the physical world. Mobius witches are powerful spell casters, occasionally using magic unfamiliar to Erebus.

Esus gifted the Svartalfar, the winter court side of the elven civil war, with a breed of large panthers that were strong mounts as well as powerful attackers in their own right. A nyxkin is a Svartalfar warrior who is bound to one of these panthers. The bond is so great that if either side dies, the other will as well.

Ogres are huge, averaging about nine feet and occasionally as large as twelve feet tall. They are unusual in that their coloration varies dramatically between individual ogres covering every end of the spectrum. Some are hairless and some are completely covered in a thick coat of fur.

Pit Beasts are tormented souls usually trapped in the chasm prisons of Camulos's hell. They are strong and mindless outside of basic animalistic urges. They have become so acclimated by pain that not only do they not fear it, but they are driven by a desire to feel it and inflict it on others.

Skeletons are formed by binding souls into the skeletal remains of a creature. Most of the time it's a human skeleton, but animals or magical beasts can also be used. Skeletons have few thoughts beyond wanting to end life and they will attack anyone they come into contact with. Necromancers have to use magic to give them an aura of the undead to keep their skeletons from attacking them. Occasionally a skeleton will become obsessed with some fragment of his former life. A skeleton may carry a teddy bear, guard the ruins of a house, or wander behind a flock of sheep.

Sometimes when an extremely corrupt and vile person dies the ground will not accept them.  Heaven and even the afterworld are closed to them; their destiny is to have their souls dragged into hell by demons. But occasionally the demons will leave them in creation. Bitter and dark, these souls turn into spectres. Eventually demons will come for them, but until then the soul has time to haunt the world.

The stygian guards are the silent servants of Hastur.  They exhibit no attempts at communication and little evidence of thought outside of their ability to ruthlessly follow commands. When they aren't being commanded they seek out pools or other bodies of water and sink unmoving to the bottom unless disturbed.

After that any good or neutral player that has researched the Honor tech can join it.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Being a member of the Overcouncil grants a significant diplomacy bonus with other members. [H1]Alignment[\\H1][PARAGRAPH:2]There are three alignments in Fall from Heaven, Good, Neutral and Evil. Each leader starts with one and some units and civics can only be used by players of a specific alignment. It also affects your diplomatic relations with other players, granting you bonuses to players of the same alignment and negatives to players of other alignments.[PARAGRAPH:2]The only way to change your alignment is by adopting a State Religion. The Order makes any player who adopts it good, the Empyrean and the Runes of Kilmorph make evil players neutral, the Council of Esus and the Undertow make good players neutral and the Ashen Veil makes the player evil.

[H1]Somnium[\\H1][PARAGRAPH:2]Somnium allows you to pick any AI leader you have contact, and aren't at war with, and challenge them to a game of cards. If you win the game you get a positive attitude bonus with that leader, if you lose you get a negative attitude penalty.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][H1]Rules[\\H1][PARAGRAPH:2]There are 10 suits with 5 cards numbered 3-7 in each. The suits are Angels, Demons, Dragons, Swords, Cups, Pentagrams, Towers, Wands, Suns and Moons. There are also 3 Fool cards and 1 Death card. [PARAGRAPH:1]The player starts his turn by drawing a card. He can draw again or stop and collect all the cards he has turned up into his "bank". The player can continue drawing as long as he wants but his turn is ended and all of his turned up cards are discarded if he ever gets 2 cards of the same suit turned up at once. Play continues back and forth between players until all 54 cards in the deck have been drawn.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][H1]Example of Play:[\\H1][PARAGRAPH:2]The player starts by turning over the 3 of Moons. He decides to draw again and draws the 6 of Wands. He decides to draw again and draws the 4 of Towers. He decides to draw again and draws the 4 of Wands. That last 4 is a duplicate, that is 2 cards of wands and all 4 cards he drew are lost and his turn is ended. If he would have stopped drawing after the 4 of Towers he would have been able to bank all 3 cards he drawn to that point and his turn would have been over.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][H1]Special Cards:[\\H1][PARAGRAPH:2]The Fool- There are three Fool cards in the deck. They allow the player to steal a card form his opponents bank and add it to the drawn card pile. If your opponent has no cards in his bank the Fool is discarded. [PARAGRAPH:1]Death- Drawing the death card automatically ends your turn and causes you to lose all your cards. There is only one death card in the deck.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][H1]Victory:[\\H1][PARAGRAPH:2]In the end each player gets points for the highest card in his bank he has of each suit (so if he has the 3, 4 and 5 of Moons he only counts the 5) and the player with the most points wins.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][H1]Strategy:[\\H1][PARAGRAPH:2]The game is about risk and deciding if you should go for that next card or not. There will be easy choices (obviously turning up a 3 of moons doesn't mean much if you already have the 5 of moons banked), and difficult ones (if your first card is the 7 of Suns should you risk it and try to get another, or just consider yourself lucky and end there). Each AI player has a different level of aggressiveness in the game, some will play conservatively, some will be more reckless.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][H1]Credits:[\\H1][NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Programmer: Stéphane "Sto" Nadry[NEWLINE]Game Designer: Derek "Kael" Paxton[NEWLINE]Art: Stephanie Pui-Mun Law and Jason Engle

[H1]Weapon Upgrades[\\H1][PARAGRAPH:2]Some units can have their strength upgraded by certain weapon types. Units capable of using [LINK=PROMOTION_BRONZE_WEAPONS]Bronze weapons[\\LINK] get +1 strength if you have access to [LINK=BONUS_COPPER]copper[\\LINK]. Units capable of using [LINK=PROMOTION_IRON_WEAPONS]Iron weapons[\\LINK] get +2 strength if you have access to [LINK=BONUS_IRON]iron[\\LINK] and units capable of using [LINK=PROMOTION_MITHRIL_WEAPONS]Mithril weapons[\\LINK] get +4 strength if you have access to [LINK=BONUS_MITHRIL]mithril[\\LINK]. Multiple weapon types aren't cumulative (a unit can't have both iron and mithril weapons) and units have to enter one of your cities to upgrade their weapons.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Note that getting access to copper requires the [LINK=TECH_BRONZE_WORKING]Bronze Working[\\LINK] tech (even though it is revealed with Mining). Getting access to Iron requires the [LINK=TECH_IRON_WORKING]Iron Working[\\LINK] tech (though it is revealed with Smelting) and getting access to Mithril requires the [LINK=TECH_MITHRIL_WORKING]Mithril Working[\\LINK] tech.

[H1]World Spells[\\H1][PARAGRAPH:2]Each civilization was a World Spell they can use. These spells have a huge effect but can only be used once per game so consider carefully before you use them. The following are the world spells for each civilization:[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Amurites- [LINK=SPELL_ARCANE_LACUNA]Arcane Lacuna[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Balseraphs- [LINK=SPELL_REVELRY]Revelry[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Bannor- [LINK=SPELL_RALLY]Rally[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Calabim- [LINK=SPELL_RIVER_OF_BLOOD]River of Blood[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Clan of Embers- [LINK=SPELL_FOR_THE_HORDE]For the Horde[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Doviello- [LINK=SPELL_WILD_HUNT]Wild Hunt[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Elohim- [LINK=SPELL_SANCTUARY]Sanctuary[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Grigori- [LINK=SPELL_ARDOR]Ardor[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Hippus- [LINK=SPELL_HIPPUS]Hippus[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Illians- [LINK=SPELL_STASIS]Stasis[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Infernal- [LINK=SPELL_HYBOREMS_WHISPER]Hyborem's Whisper[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Khazad- [LINK=SPELL_MOTHER_LODE]Mother Lode[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Kuriotates- [LINK=SPELL_LEGENDS]Legends[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Lanun- [LINK=SPELL_RAGING_SEAS]Raging Seas[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Ljosalfar- [LINK=SPELL_MARCH_OF_THE_TREES]March of the Trees[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Luchuirp- [LINK=SPELL_GIFTS_OF_NANTOSUELTA]Gifts of Nantosuelta[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Malakim- [LINK=SPELL_RELIGIOUS_FERVOR]Religious Fervor[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Mercurians- [LINK=SPELL_DIVINE_RETRIBUTION]Divine Retribution[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Sheaim- [LINK=SPELL_WORLDBREAK]Worldbreak[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Sidar- [LINK=SPELL_INTO_THE_MIST]Into the Mist[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Svartalfar- [LINK=SPELL_VEIL_OF_NIGHT]Veil of Night[\\LINK][NEWLINE][NEWLINE][TAB]Kael's Notes: We added these for two reasons. Of course they help us differentiate each of the civilizations. But we also wanted to add a strategic option where the player was forced to decide when was the best moment to use the ability. As such all of the World Spells generally grow more powerful over time, rewarding players who don't profit from there use early on.

[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Strategy: Your vampires (gained at Feudalism) can be fed either through building a couple of big farm cities, or simply by taking over enemy cities and gobbling up their entire population (bon appetit). Spread the gift to as many of your units as you can (your Moroi units can gain vampirism earlier than other unit, which usually requires level six) to allow other unit types access to this easy experience method. With their unique Breeding Pit building, the Calabim also have synergies with the slavery civic; whenever your citizens aren't being used for vampire food, they can be whipped away for production. (Your citizens may feel a bit unhappy, but they'll still be productive with a governor's manor in the city.)

[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Strategy: The Clan isn't likely to outbuild the other civs. They don't have access to special buildings and suffer a -10% to their tech rate. But this is offset by the fact that they start at peace with the barbarians so they can explore without fear and they usually don't have to worry about protecting their cities in the early game. Although they are able to attack animals, most animals will leave the clan alone, even the fearsome hill giants consider the clan their brothers and usually ignore them. With the masonry technology gained, they can double their unit production with the warrens building, and their "For the Horde!" World Spell has chance of converting any non-hero barbarian orc. A strategy of early and aggressive warfare may thus be for the best.

[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Strategy: The Doviello don't have the requirements on buildings that other civilizations do. This makes them less reliant on their cities and more able to build units in newly conquered towns. Their battlemaster unit is able to perform upgrades in the field, allowing them to keep their advance going. Charadon starts with the Barbarian trait, and its -10% research rate, while Mahala is better at researching but will find the barbarians to be less hospitable. Also, they begin with the Lucian unit, an axeman equivalent at the time of warriors and scouts. Enjoy an early conquest, you'll need it later.

[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Strategy: The Khazad are all about money. The more they have per city in their empire the bigger the bonus. Each Khazad city will have a Dwarven Vault building of various levels in it that represents this bonus. Regardless of the strategy used with the Khazad, players would do well to watch their gold amount and make sure their city expansion doesn't drop their vaults to low. They can relax a bit once they achieve Overflowing status, as their bonuses won't go up past that. Runes of Kilmorph is the best religion for making lots of money, and it should also be noted that the Khazad have better siege weapons than the other civilizations although they can't build any spellcaster units beyond adepts.

[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Strategy: The Ljosalfar are a defensive civilization-after all, they can't build any siege weapons. Instead, the Light Elves are capable of effectively mounting a war of attrition, using their forested infrastructure to overwhelm the opponent with units and pillage his lands until he's as good as dead. There are alternative methods as well-getting the Baron from the Feral Bond tech and unleashing a horde of Werewolves is an effective way of taking down enemy cities, and mages always exist. With their ability to build things in forests, the Elves have a good synergy with the Fellowship of the Leaves' forest bonuses-but a Fellowship strategy isn't strictly necessary, and following an aggressive religion like the Undertow Overlords will give good early attack units in the form of the Drown.

[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Strategy: Golems gain no experience, but a combination of the different golem-boosting buildings and Barnaxus will make them pretty mean anyway. Combine this with the fact that they're slightly more powerful than the units they replace, and you'll get a tough army, equally useful for defense and offense. Should you lose Barnaxus, you still have a chance of rebuilding him if you can kill the unit that destroyed him.

[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Strategy: Varn Gosam starts with the Creative and Spiritual traits. Quick expansion yields good results, as monuments aren't necessary for Malakim cities to expand. Cottage-spammers will enjoy this Civ, but other strategies are viable as well. Malakim units also start with the nomad promotion, allowing them to ignore the negative effect of deserts. The Malakim's World Spell will help them reach powerful priest units quickly if they spread it well and build temples beforehand.

[TAB]"Come now, people, come behold, the midget as he digs for gold!"[PARAGRAPH:1]The shout made Beeri stir from his uncomfortable sleep on the cage floor. He grudgingly started to get to his feet. The first few days of his imprisonment he had attempted to resist when the show was announced; stubbornly maintaining his lying position, but he had quickly found out that it only made things worse.[PARAGRAPH:1]He blinked against the brilliant light of the many torches lining the throne room of Perpentach, that thrice-damned carnival clown who'd taken him captive just a few weeks ago. A raiding party of merrymen had assaulted the outlying border town he had been visiting, confounding everyone with their strange dance-like fighting, and subsequently hauling Beeri off like a sack of potatoes, singing and laughing as they went.[PARAGRAPH:1]Laughter had become his worst adversary these past few days. He sometimes wished that Perpentach had just ordered him killed, or even hauled him down to some dark dungeon for torture. The harlequin seemed determined to break his spirit, and had skillfully assessed the most effective way of doing this. Or perhaps he was merely bored, Beeri could not really understand Perpentach. But his reasons were not important, as Beeri was completely certain of the one thing that mattered-he wanted to kill the man, to wipe that grotesque smile off his face once and for all.[PARAGRAPH:1]The show was about to begin. "Kilmorph, give me strength" he muttered under his breath, as Perpentach went on with his announcement:[PARAGRAPH:1]"A brilliant light in darkness shines, a piece of gold in muddy mines!"[PARAGRAPH:1]Perpentach had risen from his throne and addressed the many noblemen assembled before him, all garbed in clothes of the most bizarre shapes and colors, and most wearing masques to hide their faces. Beeri suspected that their real faces underneath might not wear quite as happy expressions as the masques-like him, they were just playing along to avoid their ruler's wrath.[PARAGRAPH:1] At the far end of Beeri's cage there was a circular hole in the floor, filled up with mud. Perpentach's preferred way of torturing him involved his diving head-first into the hole to recover a small gold-piece that had been placed there, usually near the bottom.[PARAGRAPH:1]Beeri quickly walked towards the puddle, he wanted to get this over with as fast as possible. He kneeled down and plunged his arms and head into the mud, trying to shut the laughter and applause of the gathered noblemen out of his mind. Luckily he quickly got a hold of the familiar round shape of the coin. As his hand closed around it he suddenly hesitated. Something was moving in the mud, slithering shapes. A hiss penetrated his left ear, and with a roar he threw himself backwards-still clutching the coin-seconds before the viper would have let its fangs sink into his neck. The snake hissed and slithered back into the hole.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Danger in the mines it seems, a terror from the darkest dreams"[PARAGRAPH:1]Beeri's heart was pounding. Perpentach had been creative with him before, but usually not in such a potentially fatal fashion. Perhaps it meant that he was getting bored of his new toy, and sought to dispose of him. He shrugged as he realized that the thought seemed welcome. The only thing that kept him from throwing himself back into the hole with the snake was the thought of the laughing bastard just outside the bars, and of all the creative things he could do to him given the chance.[PARAGRAPH:1]The show was not over yet, however:[PARAGRAPH:1]"The midget keeps his gold you see, if this foul beast will let him be..."[PARAGRAPH:1]Beeri whirled around as a section of wall in his cave slid away, opening a passageway he hadn't known existed. His eyes widened as he beheld the enormous hill giant that stood there, grunting furiously, and holding a club thrice the height and twice the width of Beeri's own body. He was most certainly meant to die now.[PARAGRAPH:1]Still, something deep within Beeri was not prepared to merely give in and die. He did not think of his friends and family back in the mountains, nor of his people who would most certainly be lost without him as he drew strength. All he could think of was that Perpentach meant for him to die, would draw pleasure from his death-and so it should not happen.[PARAGRAPH:1]He ignored the lumbering giant and instead dug a strong hand into the hole, grasping the writhing body of the viper. He then proceeded to fling the snake towards the giant with all his might. It landed by his left leg, and sensing a threat it immediately dug its teeth into the giant's feet. It roared with pain and fury and cracked the viper's skull with its club, but within moments it started to go into convulsions, and soon it fell flat on its back, greenish foam dripping from its mouth. Perpentach had obviously chosen a viper with a very potent venom. Ironic that it should be his savior.[PARAGRAPH:1]The crowd in the throne room applauded again, but Beeri was merely waiting for Perpentach to initiate the next death-trap. What followed surprised him, however:[PARAGRAPH:1]"The midget won the greatest prize, he proved to be both brave and wise.[PARAGRAPH:1]The game is won, the midgets foes, shall all applaud him as he goes"[PARAGRAPH:1]Perpentach gracefully walked to the door of his cage, unlocked it and opened it wide, a mysterious smile on his lips. Beeri couldn't believe his eyes. Was this another trap? He heard some of the noblemen muttering angrily, he thought he heard the phrases "...wasting a valuable hostage" and "One of his usual fancies..."[PARAGRAPH:1]Slowly Beeri started to walk. For a moment he considered assaulting Perpentach as he went out the door, grabbing his throat in an attempt to strangle him before his guards could rush to his aid. As the adrenaline rush of the battle faded, however, he started to think more clearly and realized that it would be suicide. If Perpentach was really serious about letting him go he could return in force later, and the thought of a mighty clockwork golem mashing the harlequin underfoot was enough to speed him on his way.[PARAGRAPH:1]He started to run across the floor of the throne room, looking backwards on occasion, but no one made any attempt at stopping him, and Perpentach just stood by the open prison door and smiled.[PARAGRAPH:1]Well out of Perpentach's palace, Beeri shook his head at the insanity of the place, and started to make his way home.
